newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 96/97 soybean harvest 76 pct sold-Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 96/97 soybean harvest 76 pct sold-Safras.

text.p: Brazilian farmers had sold 76 percent of the total expected 1996/97 soybean crop by the week ending May 29, independent consultants Safras e Mercado said.
This compared with 70 percent at the same stage in 1996 and an average of 62 percent over the last five years.
"Never before has the harvest been sold so rapidly in Brazil as it was this year," Safras said in a weekly report.
Assuming a total harvest of 26.02 million tonnes, this meant there were 6.2 million tonnes left to be sold, Safras said.
Forward sales were fuelled by the exceptional international prices of recent months and by strong competition in the soybean export sector, Safras said.
However, it noted sales had receded somewhat over the last three weeks, reflecting a a correction in prices on the Chicago commodities futures market.

Sales rose almost evenly in all states but reached 88 percent in Mato Grosso, where farmers attempted to secure financing early on, and only 57 percent in Rio Grande do Sul, where harvesting started later.
In view of falling international prices, Safras recommended selling the remainder of the harvest at the first price peak and investing in financial markets.

"The strategy for negotiating the rest of the Brazilian harvest must be cautious, considering the large spread between the quotations of old crop and new crop contracts on the Chicago bourse," Safras said.
Holding on to the product until just before the new Brazilian harvest was also a profitable option, although only applicable to those with no financing pressures, Safras concluded.
